title: Come, Holy Ghost, Our Hearts Inspire
description: Come, Holy Ghost, Our Hearts Inspire in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 87. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come, Ho-ly Ghost, our hearts in-spire, Let us thine in-fluence prove, Source of the old pro-phet-ic fire, Foun-tain of light and love.

lines: Come, Holy Ghost, our hearts inspire,
Source of the old prophetic fire,
Come, Holy Ghost, (for moved by thee
Unlock the truth, thyself the key,
And let there now be light.
God, through himself, we then shall know,
And sound, with all thy saints below,

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
